sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Stone County?
sections.html:
The Assessor in Galena values property, and the Collector of Revenue, also in Galena, bills and collects. Their street addresses are below.

  • Collector of Revenue: 108 E. 4th Street, P.O. Box 256, Galena, MO 65656; 417-357-6124; courthouse hours Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed on state and federal holidays.
  • Assessor: 106 E. 5th Street, P.O. Box 135, Galena, MO 65656; real estate (417) 357-6145; personal property (417) 357-6141; open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays.

The Assessor's page explains how the work is divided. The Assessor maintains the list of taxable property and closes the assessment books typically by July 1, then hands the rolls to the County Clerk, who passes them to the taxing districts. Those districts set their rates, usually by September 1, and the Assessor takes no part in rate setting.

sections.h2: When are 2026 Stone County tax bills due?
sections.html:
The 2026 statements were mailed on Friday, November 13, 2026, and online payment opened on November 6, 2026. Taxes are due by December 31 and become delinquent on January 1.

A mailed payment needs an official U.S. Post Office postmark on or before December 31 to avoid penalties and interest. The Collector's home page also lists these practical points:

  • The office no longer accepts verbal debit or credit card payments by phone. Pay in person, or call the payment number printed on the front of the statement.
  • A debit or credit card payment carries a 2.4% convenience fee, with a $1.95 minimum.
  • A drop box for tax payments is at the north entrance of the Historic Courthouse and is checked daily.
  • A paid receipt can be printed or shown on a phone at the license bureau.

Check the mailing address printed on the statement. If you need to update it, call 417-357-6124.

sections.h2: Does Stone County have a senior tax freeze?
sections.html:
The Collector lists a Senior Citizen Property Tax Credit Freeze, and its home page currently says that application process is closed. The staff directory also names a lead for the SB190 tax freeze, which is the contact to ask when the next application window opens.

State-level help is a separate matter. The Missouri Property Tax Credit Claim, filed with the Department of Revenue, is a refund for some seniors, disabled owners and renters. Ask the Collector at 417-357-6124 whether your situation fits either program before the next filing season.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Stone County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the Assessor at (417) 357-6145 and ask what the Board of Equalization deadline is for this year. RSMo 138.060 directs the county board to decide valuation appeals in a summary way, with no presumption that the assessor's value is right. When a property's assessed value rose at least 15% from the previous assessment, other than from new construction or improvement, the assessor must prove the value does not exceed true market value.

If you owe on a disputed bill, RSMo 139.031 allows payment under protest. You pay the whole bill before the delinquency date, file a written statement of your grounds with the collector, and start a circuit court action within 90 days. A taxpayer with a timely State Tax Commission appeal on file for the year does not file that separate action.

sections.h2: What if I miss the December 31 deadline in Stone County?
sections.html:
The bill goes delinquent on January 1, and penalties and interest begin. RSMo 140.150 allows delinquent land to be sold on the fourth Monday in August. Before publication, the collector mails notices to the owner of record, and the owner can pay the tax, penalty, interest and costs at any time before the sale.

A seller with a bill outstanding should arrange payment through closing. Ask the Collector for the exact payoff, since penalties change by date, and give that figure to the title company. The Collector accepts payment in person at its Galena office and in the courthouse drop box.

sections.h2: How fast is Stone County growing?
sections.html:
Population is rising. The Census Bureau's estimate base for April 2020 was 31,079, and the July 2025 estimate is 32,503, a rise of 4.6%. Over the same period St. Louis County and Stoddard County each fell 1.4%. Stone County was part of the Branson micropolitan area until 2023, and Branson West Municipal Airport is a public-use airport two nautical miles west of Branson West.

Density is 67.0 people per square mile on 463.83 square miles of land. Median gross rent is $896, and median selected monthly owner costs are $1,451 with a mortgage and $476 without. About 88.1% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Of adults 25 and older, 91.8% finished high school and 24.8% hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

The Census lists 21,225 housing units for July 2025 and 13,530 households for 2020 to 2024, so the housing stock is well above the count of households. When you set a price, compare your parcel with sales of similar houses in your own community and school district rather than leaning on the county median of $249,000.

sections.h2: What is Stone County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Stone County lies in southwest Missouri along the Arkansas line, bordered by Christian, Taney, Barry and Lawrence counties and by Carroll County, Arkansas. Galena is the seat, and Kimberling City is the largest city. Branson West, Reeds Spring, Crane, Hurley and Blue Eye are also in or near the county, and part of Mark Twain National Forest lies within it. Water covers 47 of its 511 square miles, or 9.2%.

The county grew from 9,921 residents in 1970 to 31,076 in 2020. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 32,503. The QuickFacts table gives the housing picture.

faqs.q: Where is the Stone County Collector's office?
faqs.a: At 108 E. 4th Street in Galena, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 256, Galena, MO 65656. The phone is 417-357-6124, and the courthouse is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Stone County tax by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, in person or online, and by calling the payment number on your statement. The Collector lists a 2.4% convenience fee with a $1.95 minimum, and verbal card payments by phone are no longer taken.

faqs.q: When do Stone County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On January 1. They are due by December 31, and a mailed payment needs a U.S. Post Office postmark on or before that date.

faqs.q: Who sets the tax rate in Stone County?
faqs.a: The taxing jurisdictions do, usually by September 1. The Assessor values property and is not part of rate setting, according to the county's Assessor page.

faqs.q: Is the senior tax freeze application open?
faqs.a: The Collector's home page says the Senior Citizen Property Tax Credit Freeze application process is closed. Call 417-357-6124 to ask when it opens again.
